newsitem.title: USA: Poll shows support for Florida sugar tax.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows support for Florida sugar tax.

text.p: Forty-nine percent of likely Florida voters support a proposed penny-a-pound tax on sugar growers, while 40 percent oppose it and 11 percent are undecided, according to a poll published Thursday.
The Mason-Dixon Political/Media Research poll was conducted for several Florida news organizations. It was based on interviews with 805 likely voters and has an error margin of 3.5 percentage points.
Poll director Robert Joffee cautioned that election results could be much closer because undecided voters tend to vote "no" on tax issues.
"Proposals such as this one often lose support and only rarely gain support during the final stretch of a campaign," Joffee said.

The constitutional amendment levying the tax on sugarcane growers appears on the Nov 5 ballot. The tax would raise about $225 million a year to clean up Everglades pollution caused by fertilizer-laden water that runs off the sugarcane farms into the sensitive wetlands.
Related amendments on the Nov 5 ballot would create a trust fund to hold the revenues and require that anyone polluting the Everglades be primarily responsible for paying the cost of abatement.
The poll showed 59 percent of likely votes favor the trust fund and 72 percent support making polluters pay for cleanup.
Another consitutional amendment could put the outcome fo the sugar tax proposal in doubt if it passes by less than a two-thirds majority.
Amendment One, also on the Nov 5 ballot, would require two-thirds voter approval, rather than a simple majority, for any tax increase adopted by referendum.
The Mason-Dixon poll showed 54 percent of voters favor that amendment. If it passes, the courts would have to decide whether the two-thirds requirement applies to a tax enacted the same day.
